# Eva Yuan

# Data Frame Transformations

1. Joins
2. Pivot/Unpivot

# Example

### Dataframe  Setup


```{python}
#| echo: TRUE

# Load data as a polars dataframe

import polars as pl



df_customers = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "customer_id": [1, 2, 3],
        "name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"],
    }
)
print(df_customers)


df_orders = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "order_id": ["a", "b", "c"],
        "customer_id": [1, 2, 2],
        "amount": [100, 200, 300],
    }
)
print(df_orders)


```

## Demo 1: Inner Join

```{python}

df_inner_customer_join = df_customers.join(df_orders, on="customer_id", how="inner")
print(df_inner_customer_join)

# only joins tables with the same column. in this case it's "customer_id"

```

## Demo 2: Left Join

```{python}

df_left_join = df_customers.join(df_orders, on="customer_id", how="left")
print(df_left_join)

# in a left join, the table on the left gets to keep all columns/observations. in this case it's "df_customers".

```

## Demo 3: Right Join

```{python}

df_right_join = df_orders.join(df_customers, on="customer_id", how="right")
print(df_right_join)

# in a right join, the table on the right gets to keep all columns/observations. in this case it's "df_customers".

```


## Demo 4: Full (Outer) Join

```{python}

df_outer_join = df_customers.join(df_orders, on="customer_id", how="full")
print(df_outer_join)

```



## Demo 5: Semi Join


### Setup
```{python}

df_cars = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": ["a", "b", "c"],
        "make": ["ford", "toyota", "bmw"],
    }
)
print(df_cars)



df_repairs = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "id": ["c", "c"],
        "cost": [100, 200],
    }
)
print(df_repairs)


```

### Semi-join demo

```{python}

df_semi_join = df_cars.join(df_repairs, on="id", how="semi")
print(df_semi_join)



```

### Demo 6: Anti-join

```{python}

df_anti_join = df_cars.join(df_repairs, on="id", how="anti")
print(df_anti_join)


```




## Pivot

### Data setup
```{python}

df = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "foo": ["A", "A", "B", "B", "C"],
        "N": [1, 2, 2, 4, 2],
        "bar": ["k", "l", "m", "n", "o"],
    }
)
print(df)

```

### Pivot demo

```{python}

out = df.pivot("bar", index="foo", values="N", aggregate_function="first")
print(out)

```



## Unpivot

### Data setup

```{python}

df2 = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "A": ["a", "b", "a"],
        "B": [1, 3, 5],
        "C": [10, 11, 12],
        "D": [2, 4, 6],
    }
)
print(df2)


```


### Unpivot

```{python}

out2 = df2.unpivot(["C", "D"], index=["A", "B"])
print(out2)


```
